title: fix(story): exclude flowless guides from the opening clock
body:
## Problem and value

Flowless guides were counted as Story opening events. On the bundled waterfall, their synthetic travel stretched the opening from the node horizon of 1.9 seconds to 3.2589 seconds; a longer guide could speed up the establish shot unnecessarily.

The opening clock now counts only edges with an actual native transfer. Flowless guides retain their fallback travel when a later scene traces them, and real transfers still extend the opening. This is a Story timing correction; authored diagram geometry is unchanged.

## Integration and scope

#1036 has already merged. Its ranged-audio correction and current dev's newer FFmpeg diagnostics remain in the base. This PR now contains only the remaining opening-clock fix, its browser regression, and the canonical archive.

Final head `a1433505d2f67c59fc9a587dfe409d9ad7a9d188` preserves contributor head `b29fa4ae8e6ec411d1e4bb1309b2adef5ddd45d6` and merges dev `82c7e0f089a02a4d514714adf37dc2061682da5f`. Relative to dev: three source-line additions/two removals in `archify/story/story.js`, 37 browser-test lines, and `archify.zip`. The archive's only changed entry is `archify/story/story.js`.

## Validation

- Current-dev control fails the existing focused browser regression: waterfall opening span 3.258903394426618 versus node horizon 1.9. The candidate passes, including the extended flowless guide and real-transfer workflow controls.
- Final source: Story browser, Story node and release-package checks — 60 passed, 2 platform skips, 0 failed. Real Chrome and FFmpeg 9.0.2/ffprobe were configured; existing early/late ranged-video audio decode checks executed.
- `npm run test:generated` and `git diff --check` passed. Official Node 22.23.3 / zlib 1.3.1-e00f703 produced the archive. Viewer/gallery/example inputs are unchanged, so their outputs required no additional refresh.
- Hosted CI must be assessed on this published final head. Local runtime assertions establish timing and decode behavior; they are not a new human visual sign-off.

The scoped improvement check found no additional abstraction or test expansion worthwhile inside this timing correction.

## AI assistance and accountability

Original follow-up: Cursor Grok 4.7, accountable contributor @tt-a1i, retaining the #1036 contributor history. Maintainer update: Codex (`gpt-6.1-sol`) reviewed the current scope, integrated dev, verified the regression and real decoder, regenerated the archive, and updated this description.

- [ ] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them. Validation results and gaps are recorded above.

## Apache-base integration (2026-10-25)

Normal merge of frozen dev `3f95f0349c8276db71509ca239461b6fe9d00f9f`; candidate `82faee7567769f6496315ae289ee331e4dd22849`. Retains original contributor history, the scoped opening-clock fix and current Apache/historical-MIT/NOTICE/third-party notice files. Only ZIP conflicted and was rebuilt from the combined tracked source.

Official Node 22.23.3: focused real-Chrome flowless-opening regression 1 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip; Story unit/public-CLI suite 21 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip; standalone software-notice regression passed. Independent Story attachment probe verifies exact notice text in both the outer retained native HTML and the embedded Story HTML. Canonical ZIP double build is byte-identical; extracted package notice files match source and package smoke passes without dependencies.

Prior actual FFmpeg 9.0.2/ffprobe ranged-audio decode evidence at a1433505 is reused at its original identity: Story timing/audio/export/webm source files are byte-identical, while this merge's Story tool addition is nonvisual notice data. No new decoder result or human visual sign-off is claimed. Current opening/attachment behavior was checked on this candidate. Final CI remains required on the combined integration revision. No release or live installation.
